newsitem.title: JAPAN: Japan police to guard emperor on L.America tour.
newsitem.headline: Japan police to guard emperor on L.America tour.

text.p: Alarmed by the Lima hostage crisis, Japan will send its own police guard with Emperor Akihito and Empress Michiko when they visit Latin America later this week.
It will be the first time for Japanese police to accompany the royal couple on a trip overseas, highlighting increased security worries in the wake of the Peru hostage drama.

A police spokesman told reporters on Thursday that six officers would guard the imperial couple during the two-week tour of Brazil and Argentina starting on Friday, breaking with the past practice of using guards from the Imperial Household Agency.

Marxist rebels took over the Japanese ambassador's residence in Lima last December in an attack to win the release of jailed comrades and to protest against what they regarded as Japanese economic interference in the country's affairs.
Japan also has extensive investments in Brazil and Argentina.
The Lima siege ended four months later when Peruvian commandos stormed the residence, killing all 14 rebels and freeing alive all but one of the 72 remaining hostages.
